profile_text.body:
EleutherAI is a nonprofit organization, headquartered remotely, that describes its work as AI research. According to its site, it aims to address the problem that as models get smarter, humans will not always be able to independently check whether a model's claims are true or false, and it says it works on directly eliciting latent knowledge (ELK) inside a model's activations.

The site also describes research on test set contamination. EleutherAI writes that as frontier AI systems are pretrained on web-scale data, contamination has become a critical concern for accurately assessing capabilities, and that while the impact on discriminative evaluations such as multiple-choice question-answering has been studied thoroughly, comparatively little work has examined generative evaluations. In the work described, language models were pretrained on mixtures of web data and the MATH benchmark, sweeping model sizes and the number of test set replicas contaminating the pretraining corpus, with performance improving with contamination and model size. Using scaling laws, the company reports finding that including even a single test set replica enables models to achieve lower results, with the site text ending there.

No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
